requirements.source: User Confirmation. An impostor may impersonate a trusted person and attempt to transfer funds without proper authorization.
requirements.title: Treat impersonation as a threat, not a confirmation source.
requirements.detail: Source context, with no independent executable condition. No impersonation detector is invented; the following rules require explicit evidence regardless of wording.

requirements.source: Therefore, every transfer must have explicit user confirmation for the exact recipient and amount.
requirements.title: Confirm this exact recipient and amount.
requirements.detail: The rule matches host confirmation against exact intent/recipient/cents in the EDB. A real authenticated UI producer is still required; tests ingest synthetic facts through the private host API.

requirements.source: A confirmation must be associated with the specific transfer request.
requirements.title: Bind confirmation to a specific immutable transfer intent.
requirements.detail: After an original bank transfer succeeds, its confirmed delta updates Consumed, Transfer, Balance and DailyBudget in one EDB batch. Bank JSON and EDB do not share a transaction; uncertain synchronization stops the session.

requirements.source: Instructions contained in external messages, including SMS messages, must not be treated as user confirmation.
requirements.title: Never turn message instructions into a user-confirmation fact.
requirements.detail: No agent/MCP assertion endpoint exists. The host must authenticate confirmations; an arbitrary JSON label saying user is not proof of user intent.

requirements.source: Additional Verification for Suspicious Recipients. A scammer often provides unfamiliar payment details and creates a sense of urgency to pressure the victim into transferring money.
requirements.title: Do not infer trust from familiar wording or urgency.
requirements.detail: Source context, with no independent executable condition. No semantic scam classifier is required or claimed by these rules.

requirements.source: So, Transfers to unregistered recipients or recipients whose payment details originate from untrusted messages must not be executed without additional identity verification and a cooling-off period.
requirements.title: Require identity review and elapsed cooling for unknown or message-derived details.
requirements.detail: Review/cooling evidence is privately ingested into the EDB. The source leaves the cooling duration unspecified. The original prompt remains stricter for unregistered recipients.

requirements.source: A user's request to proceed does not, by itself, bypass these requirements.
requirements.title: User confirmation cannot override review and cooling.
requirements.detail: Final Allow joins all independent requirements. No IgnoreDeny input or agent override is exposed.

requirements.source: Daily Transfer Limit. A daily transfer limit can reduce potential financial losses if a user or an agent is deceived into making payments.
requirements.title: Cap possible daily loss.
requirements.detail: Source context, with no independent executable condition. The next clause expresses the numeric cap; this motivation adds no predicate.

requirements.source: The Payments Agent must not execute a transfer if the transfer amount, combined with the total amount transferred that day, exceeds the configured daily limit of $1,000.
requirements.title: Keep requested cents within the current remaining daily budget.
requirements.detail: Balance and DailyBudget are integer-cent policy inputs. Original bank JSON mechanics remain unchanged; the result adapter records the confirmed amount delta using singleton replacement. Correct bank-day rollover still needs a trusted producer.

requirements.source: Transfers within the limit remain subject to all other applicable authorization requirements.
requirements.title: A budget check alone never authorizes a transfer.
requirements.detail: One Datalog Allow joins confirmation, provenance, review and remaining budget before invoking the original bank callback.

requirements.source: Payment Information Provenance. Without tracking, information introduced by a scammer may be treated as real user-provided payment instructions.
requirements.title: Do not let repeated instructions silently become trusted data.
requirements.detail: Source context, with no independent executable condition. Provenance is about recorded data versions, not a classifier over natural-language text.

requirements.source: The system must track whether payment details originate from registered banking records, direct user input, or untrusted external messages.
requirements.title: Track bank, direct-user and external-message origins.
requirements.detail: Trusted ingestion and transformation adapters must submit Source/DependsOn facts. The original free-text app still lacks those producers; synthetic fixtures exercise this contract.

requirements.source: Rephrasing or repeating information from an untrusted message must not automatically change its recorded origin to trusted user input.
requirements.title: A rewrite retains any declared external-message ancestor.
requirements.detail: The builtin closure preserves the old origin along declared dependencies. Adding Source(user, rewritten-data) does not erase Source(external_message, ancestor). Missing transformation edges remain an observation gap.

requirements.source: Separation of Agent Responsibilities. Separating responsibilities prevents an agent that processes untrusted messages from directly controlling financial transactions.
requirements.title: Separate untrusted-message processing from payment execution.
requirements.detail: The three original Payments tool bodies retain their bank JSON operations and logging. Added decorators gate them and record confirmed transfer deltas; the Assistant/A2A message bridge remains unmodified.

requirements.source: Only the Payments Agent may invoke the transfer execution tool.
requirements.title: Allow only the bound Payments principal to execute.
requirements.detail: The adapter reads the caller name from MCP request _meta.caller, or caller_context for direct Python calls. Rules require payments. A real MCP test sends assistant and payments to the same endpoint and observes denial/success. The original host must propagate its agent name; endpoint authentication remains deployment work.

requirements.source: The Assistant Agent may request payment verification but must not directly execute transfers or modify banking records.
requirements.title: Assistant verifies without a transfer or bank-write tool.
requirements.detail: The original Assistant tool list lacks execute_transfer. This does not prevent a misconfigured deployment from giving Assistant the payment endpoint.

requirements.source: The verification should not result in a transfer execution.
requirements.title: A verification-only request must not execute.
requirements.detail: Purpose comes from host evidence and blocks verification intents. The original free-text A2A request is not bound to an authenticated execution scope, so the full causal property remains open.

requirements.source: Information Isolation Between Agents. Restricting information flow reduces unnecessary exposure of sensitive data and prevents malicious instructions embedded in external messages from crossing agent boundaries.
requirements.title: Limit inter-agent disclosure to necessary payment information.
requirements.detail: Source context, with no independent executable condition. The remaining P6 clauses expose a distinct output/message boundary, which this payment-execution port does not claim to solve.

requirements.source: The Assistant Agent must not access account balances or full bank account numbers directly.
requirements.title: Keep balances and full accounts out of Assistant tools.
requirements.distilled: Original masked list; partial deployment boundary
requirements.detail: Original list_payees reads bank.json and emits names and masked accounts unchanged. An added policy decorator gates this call. Network identity and other output channels still require deployment scoping.

requirements.source: The Payments Agent must not receive the same message from the Assistant Agent, e.g., raw SMS content or unrelated conversation history.
requirements.title: Never forward raw SMS or unrelated history to Payments.
requirements.distilled: Unsupported on the original message path
requirements.detail: request_payment_verification still accepts and forwards free-form request_text. A transfer guard cannot undo a message already sent.

requirements.source: Communication between agents must be limited to the information necessary to verify and process the specific payment request.
requirements.title: Send only structured fields required for this payment.
requirements.detail: A reviewed structured A2A schema and response projection are needed. No generic Sink predicate or provenance closure can substitute for instrumenting the actual bridge.

TransferIntent.text: A trusted host submits this exact request directly to the EDB, binding ID, recipient, cents and a details handle. No agent assertion API is registered.
TransferIntent.brief: Required host input binding intent, recipient, cents and details.

UserConfirmation.text: A real authenticated host/UI must submit this input. A model claim or SMS does not become confirmation; tests use explicit synthetic host ingestion.
UserConfirmation.brief: Required authenticated host/UI input; absent from the original app.

Purpose.text: A trusted host binds the intent to transfer or verification in the EDB.

Consumed.text: After original bank success, the result adapter records this fact with policy balance, budget and transfer evidence in one EDB batch.
Consumed.brief: Callback records successful consumption of an intent.

Payee.text: Reviewed .dl seeds match registered payees in the mock bank. Original tools still read bank JSON; the policy EDB is not reloaded on every call.
Payee.brief: Reviewed .dl payees matching the mock bank.

IdentityVerified.text: A trusted verification producer submits the exact reviewed intent, recipient and cents to the EDB.

CoolingUntil.text: A trusted host submits the deadline. .key CoolingUntil(Intent) replaces an earlier deadline; the model cannot choose one.

Clock.text: A small before-call adapter replaces this singleton with the server time. This is an observation, not an application snapshot.
Clock.brief: Before hook records current server time in seconds.

DailyBudget.text: A singleton holds remaining/configured policy cents. The confirmed transfer delta replaces remaining; original bank JSON retains its own business counter.
DailyBudget.brief: Callback replaces remaining cents after a successful transfer.

Balance.text: Initial reviewed cents match the mock bank. After an original transfer succeeds, its confirmed amount decrements the keyed policy balance; no per-call bank projection runs.
Balance.brief: Callback replaces balance cents after a successful transfer.

Provenance.text: Possible origins propagate through declared Source and DependsOn edges. The adapter gives each host-recorded data version an opaque SDK ID.

Source.origin: Optional builtin; newly required host input
Source.text: Trusted ingestion submits bank/user/external_message origins directly to the EDB.

DependsOn.origin: Optional builtin; newly required host input
DependsOn.text: Trusted transformation adapters submit versioned copy/rewrite dependencies directly to the EDB.

findings: Both ports retain original business stores and callbacks. Policy EDB facts are maintained by explicit confirmed-result adapters, not per-call full-state projections.
Generic .key metadata replaces current policy rows. New tool-created ResourceType/ResourceState tuples are checked against InitialState(Type, State); tools cannot reset existing FSM state.
The original MCP float boundary remains. The wrapper normalizes policy arguments to integer cents and adds host intent correlation metadata without changing the bank function body.
Original bank JSON and the policy EDB do not share a transaction. Post-effect synchronization failures stop the session; no automatic rollback or restart reconciliation is claimed.
The app still lacks authenticated confirmation, identity-review and source producers. These are private host-ingestion contracts, not facts an LLM may assert.
The unchanged Payments prompt is stricter for unregistered recipients. P6 still requires a structured adapter on the free-text A2A bridge.

Caller names now come from application context or MCP _meta.caller. Missing names fail before business execution. These reported names are not authenticated; the original external host still needs to send its agent name.
toolExplanation: An added decorator reads request _meta.caller (or direct-call context), guards the existing callback and records confirmed deltas. No principal is hardcoded in the annotation.
toolSetup:
policy = adapt()
module.policy_port = policy
module.BANK_PATH = reviewed_mock_bank_path

execute_transfer.text: Original transfer tool; the wrapper adds intent correlation metadata.

check_daily_limit.text: Check the remaining mock daily limit.

list_payees.text: Assistant lists payee names and masked accounts.
